items.q: Why WhatsApp rather than an app?
items.a: Because your guests and your teams already use it. A housekeeper will not install a business app, and neither will a traveling guest. WhatsApp removes the hurdle: no account to create, nothing to download, no forgotten password.

items.q: Does the assistant answer guests on its own?
items.a: It handles routine requests and suggests replies for the rest. You set what goes out automatically and what goes through approval. The level of autonomy is yours: we do not assume an AI should handle everything without human oversight.

items.q: Do I need a WhatsApp Business number?
items.a: Yes, the property uses its own business number through the WhatsApp Business API. Setting it up is part of the rollout.

items.q: In which languages do teams receive their tasks?
items.a: In French or Arabic, depending on what each person actually uses. It is a point often overlooked: a tool that only the front desk understands leaves the field outside the system, when the field is what executes.

items.q: Can the police form be collected through WhatsApp?
items.a: Yes. The guest fills it in before arrival and attaches their ID document, as part of the digital check-in. You get complete data without typing at the desk. Declaring to the authorities remains your own procedure.

items.q: What happens if a guest writes at night?
items.a: The assistant answers routine requests at any hour and escalates the rest according to your rules. The point is not to reply fast for the sake of it, but for every request to be handled or escalated, without waiting for the morning.

items.q: Is the Sojori PMS mandatory?
items.a: No. Sojori includes its own PMS for a property that does not have one, but it also connects to existing PMSs, including Mews. You can therefore add the orchestration layer without touching your booking system: it is often the shortest way to measure what it brings.

items.q: Does it handle the Moroccan police form?
items.a: Sojori takes care of the form: the guest fills it in and signs it before arrival from WhatsApp, with their ID document, as part of the digital check-in. You get complete data without typing at the desk. Declaring to the authorities remains the property’s own procedure.

items.q: How is the tourist tax calculated?
items.a: It is set per property: an amount per guest and per night. Sojori calculates the amount; collection follows the mode you set.

items.q: Can I manage several properties?
items.a: Yes, with a consolidated view and rules specific to each site. This is usually where a PMS designed for a single property reaches its limit: shared teams, priority trade-offs between sites, overall reporting.

items.q: What happens to our booking history?
items.a: Data migration is handled during onboarding. It is the longest step of the rollout, and the one to scope first, more than the installation itself.

items.q: How long until we are operational?
items.a: A few days for a single property. What takes time is not going live but migrating the history and setting up your rules: cleaning cadences, pricing, approval paths.

privacy.intro: At Sojori, your privacy is our priority. This policy explains what personal data we collect, why we collect it, how we use it and the rights you have over it.

sections.title: 1. Data We Collect
sections.content:
We collect the minimum data necessary to provide and improve the service:

• Contact details (name, email, phone) provided during sign-up or demo requests.
• Business information (company name, number of properties, role) shared when engaging with our services.
• Guest data (names, passport scans, contact details) processed on behalf of our users for check-in and identity verification.
• Technical data (IP address, browser type, device, access logs) collected automatically for security and performance.

sections.title: 2. How We Use Your Data
sections.content:
Your data is used to:

• Provide and operate the Sojori platform.
• Process demo requests and appointment scheduling.
• Send transactional notifications (booking confirmations, task alerts).
• Improve service quality, fix bugs and develop new features.
• Ensure platform security and prevent fraud.
• Comply with legal and regulatory requirements.

We do not sell or rent your personal data to third parties for marketing purposes.

sections.title: 3. Data Sharing
sections.content:

• With infrastructure providers (Google Cloud, MongoDB Atlas, AWS) that process data on our behalf under strict contractual safeguards.
• With integrated services (WhatsApp Business API, Channex, Rentals United) to the extent required for their operation.
• With legal authorities when required by law or court order.

All sub-processors are bound by data-processing agreements compliant with GDPR and Moroccan data-protection law.

• Strictly necessary cookies to enable core functionality.
• Performance cookies to analyse website usage (anonymised).
• Optional cookies for personalisation.

You can manage cookie preferences through your browser settings at any time.

Account data is retained for the duration of the subscription plus six (6) months. Guest data processed on behalf of users is retained according to the user's settings and applicable local regulations.

Under GDPR and Moroccan law (Loi 09-08), you have the right to:

• Access the personal data we hold about you.
• Rectify inaccurate or incomplete data.
• Request deletion of your data (right to be forgotten).
• Restrict or object to certain processing.
• Data portability — receive your data in a structured, machine-readable format.
• Withdraw consent for optional processing at any time.

To exercise these rights, contact us at support@sojori.com. We will respond within thirty (30) days.

items.q: What is Sojori, in one sentence?
items.a: The orchestration engine for hospitality: it orchestrates a property's guest experience, operations and revenue by connecting systems, guests, teams and partners.

items.q: How is it different from a PMS?
items.a: A PMS records the state of a stay; an orchestrator triggers what should follow from it. Sojori includes its own PMS, but it also connects to existing PMS, so you don't have to replace what you have in order to orchestrate.

items.q: Where is Sojori available?
items.a: Morocco first (Marrakech, Casablanca, Rabat, Tangier, Agadir), then France. This is no accident: the police registration form, the tourist tax and Arabic as a working language are built in, whereas an international platform treats them as special cases.

items.q: Who is Sojori for?
items.a: Hotels, riads, guesthouses and residences. Orchestration is most valuable when there are flows to coordinate: teams, simultaneous arrivals, several channels. For a very small property run by two people, a good PMS may be enough.

items.q: Does Sojori replace Cloudbeds?
items.a: Not necessarily. Sojori includes its own PMS, but it also connects to existing PMS: you can keep Cloudbeds for reservations and add the orchestration layer on top. This is a fundamental difference from the other alternatives, which all require a complete replacement.

items.q: What is the real difference between the two?
items.a: The scope. Cloudbeds centralizes stay information; Sojori triggers what follows from it. Put differently: Cloudbeds tells you room 12 has been vacated, while Sojori sends the housekeeping task to the right person, follows up if nobody picks it up, and alerts you if the next arrival risks having to wait.

items.q: Does Cloudbeds handle the Moroccan police registration form?
items.a: We don't comment on the exact scope of a competitor's product, which changes over time. Ask them directly, and request a demonstration on your own case: a form collected before arrival, in Arabic, with the ID document. You will see right away what each tool can do.

items.q: Is migration complicated?
items.a: It is taken care of. And if you prefer not to migrate, connecting to your current PMS remains possible. It is often the shortest path to measure what orchestration brings before deciding anything about your reservation system.

items.q: How long does it take to be up and running?
items.a: A few days for a single property. What takes time is never the installation but transferring the history and setting up the rules specific to your operation: housekeeping schedules, pricing rules, approval circuits.

items.q: Is Sojori listed under Go Siyaha?
items.a: We do not claim any accreditation we cannot document, and to date we do not display one. Nozoul does display a listing under the program: that is a real advantage for a hotelier putting together an application, and we would rather tell you so. If funding is your deciding criterion, ask Maroc PME before choosing.

items.q: What is the concrete difference from a standard PMS?
items.a: A PMS waits for data to be entered; an orchestrator triggers. A confirmed departure generates the housekeeping task, a room reported as faulty opens a ticket, an approaching stay sends its messages. In a quiet property the difference is small. On a day with twenty departures, it is visible.

items.q: Can I keep my current PMS?
items.a: Yes, it is often the shortest path. Sojori connects to existing PMS, including Mews, retrieves reservations and room statuses, and orchestrates around them. You measure the benefit without putting your reservation system at risk.

items.q: Does Sojori handle the police registration form and the tourist tax?
items.a: Yes. The form is collected before arrival: the guest fills it in from WhatsApp with their ID document. Sojori calculates the tourist tax per guest and per night, according to each unit's setting. Declaring to the authorities remains your responsibility.

items.q: What if my property is small?
items.a: Then compare honestly, and look first at price and simplicity. Orchestration is most valuable when there are teams to coordinate. For a six-room riad run by two people, a good PMS may be enough. We would rather tell you that than sell you an oversized tool.

items.q: Do I need to replace Pluriel to use Sojori?
items.a: Not necessarily. Sojori connects to existing PMS; depending on the integration options of your setup, orchestration can be added without touching your reservation system. This has to be examined case by case, so let's talk before considering a migration.

items.q: What happens to the reservation history?
items.a: Data transfer is taken care of during setup. It is generally the longest step of the rollout, and the one to scope first.

items.q: Is the cloud reliable when the connection is unstable?
items.a: That is the right question to ask, and it deserves an honest answer: a prolonged outage affects access. That is the historic argument for installed software. In practice, orchestration goes largely through WhatsApp on your teams' phones, which work on mobile data independently of the property's wifi.

items.q: Pluriel does accounting and payroll. Does Sojori too?
items.a: No. Sojori orchestrates operations: reservations, housekeeping, maintenance, guest relations, revenue. Accounting and payroll are outside its scope, and exports feed your accounting tool. If you are looking for a complete administrative suite from a single vendor, the Pluriel suite covers ground that we do not.

items.q: Does Sojori speak Arabic?
items.a: Yes, and it is central. Tasks sent to field teams go out in French or Arabic, on WhatsApp, with no app to install and no account to create.

items.q: Does Sojori replace Welcomax?
items.a: It can, since it includes a PMS. But it can also be added alongside it if the integration allows: Sojori connects to existing PMS, retrieves reservations and room statuses, and orchestrates around them. It is often the shortest path to measure the benefit before any migration decision.

items.q: What is the fundamental difference?
items.a: The scope. A PMS suite centralizes information; an orchestrator triggers the actions that follow from it. Knowing that the room has been vacated, or making sure it is ready before the next arrival: these are not the same products.

items.q: Both handle Moroccan compliance, so where is the gap?
items.a: In when the data is collected. With Sojori, the police registration form is filled in by the guest before arrival, from WhatsApp, with their ID document, and the front desk enters nothing. The gap is not in the document produced, it is in the work avoided.

items.q: And pricing?
items.a: Sojori manages pricing through rules, keeping the calculation algorithmic and flagging recommendations rather than applying them blindly, with minimum and maximum limits. This is a deliberate choice: we do not let a model set your prices on its own.

items.q: How do I compare the two seriously?
items.a: Ask both vendors for the same demonstration, on a real scenario from your property: a departure at 11 am, an early arrival at 1 pm, a room reported as faulty, a guest writing in Arabic. In fifteen minutes you will see what each tool actually does.

items.q: Which indicators should I track first?
items.a: Occupancy rate, average rate and revenue per available room, but above all by period, by category and by channel, never as an overall average. A monthly average hides exactly what needs fixing: the weekend dip in Casablanca, the low season in Tangier.

items.q: Can I see non-accommodation revenue?
items.a: Yes. Food and beverage, spa, transfers, upgrades and late departures are tracked separately. It is often the least well measured part of an operation, even though it grows when guest relations are orchestrated.

items.q: Is the data up to date?
items.a: Operating indicators (arrivals, departures, room status, pending messages) reflect the current situation. Revenue analyses are consolidated over the chosen period.

items.q: Can we export to our accounting?
items.a: Yes, exports are available to feed your accounting tool. Sojori is not accounting software and does not try to replace it: it provides the operating data.

items.q: How do I compare several properties?
items.a: Reporting consolidates the sites while allowing them to be compared with each other: occupancy, average rate, channel mix, revenue per available room. This is what tools designed for a single property do poorly.

items.q: What is the best PMS for a hotel in Morocco?
items.a: The question is poorly framed, and that is what wastes time. There is no best PMS in the absolute: there is a product suited to your size, your organization and your real problem. A six-room riad run by two people and a group of four properties with thirty employees do not have the same needs. Start by identifying what costs you the most today (entering reservations, coordinating teams, or distribution on the OTA) and then compare on that point.

items.q: What is the difference between a PMS and an orchestration engine?
items.a: A PMS records and centralizes: reservations, rooms, invoices, channels. An orchestration engine triggers what follows from it: a confirmed departure generates the housekeeping task, a room reported as faulty opens a maintenance ticket, an approaching stay sends its messages to the guest. In a quiet property, the difference is hardly noticeable. On a day with twenty departures, it decides whether the rooms are ready on time.

items.q: Should I choose Moroccan or international software?
items.a: A local vendor handles the police registration form, the tourist tax, the dirham and Arabic natively, whereas an international platform handles them as local variants. In return, international platforms often offer broader integration ecosystems. If your operation is entirely Moroccan, local roots weigh heavily. If you operate in several countries, the trade-off reverses.

items.q: Cloud or on-premise?
items.a: The cloud opens from a browser, updates for everyone and requires no server or backups to watch over. On-premise remains accessible during an internet outage and allows deep hardware integration: door locks, phone systems, time clocks. Today most new deployments are cloud-based, but a project with a heavy infrastructure component may justify the other choice.

items.q: What is the Go Siyaha programme?
items.a: Go Siyaha is a Moroccan public programme led by the Ministry of Tourism and rolled out by the Maroc PME agency. It aims to modernise and digitalise the tourism sector: accommodation, restaurants, travel agencies and tourist transport. It rests on three pillars: investment support, green growth, and digital transformation with technical assistance.

items.q: What is the subsidy rate for digitalisation?
items.a: Professional sources in the sector report coverage of up to 90% of expenses for expertise, consulting, marketing and digital transformation, against 30 to 40% for physical investments such as works and equipment. The exact rates, ceilings and conditions that apply to your application must be confirmed with Maroc PME, the only body entitled to set them.

items.q: Is my property eligible?
items.a: The programme targets Moroccan private-law companies with 100% private capital operating in tourism, with annual turnover excluding tax below 200 million dirhams on average over the last three financial years. Since July 2025, the size barriers have been lifted: very small businesses, guesthouses, cooperatives and young project owners are eligible, and the minimum investment threshold has been removed. Check your situation with Maroc PME.

items.q: Is hotel management software an eligible expense?
items.a: The digital transformation component covers expertise, consulting, marketing and digital tools: website, booking engine, search visibility, brand identity. Some players in the sector indicate that PMS and channel manager solutions fall within this scope. Sojori does not rule on the eligibility of your application: Maroc PME reviews it and decides.

items.q: Is Sojori approved or listed under Go Siyaha?
items.a: We do not claim any approval that we cannot document. If you are putting together a Go Siyaha application, we provide what your file needs from our side: a detailed quote, a functional description, the deployment scope. You remain in charge of the process with Maroc PME. Ask them whether a provider needs to be listed.

items.q: How do you put together an application?
items.a: The process goes through Maroc PME. The documents usually requested are the commercial register extract, the ICE, the articles of association, the financial statements for the last three financial years, a business plan and supplier quotes. We can send you a detailed quote matching the scope you have in mind; the rest of the application is up to you and your advisor.

items.q: Does the guest need to install anything?
items.a: No. Everything goes through WhatsApp, which they already use: confirmation, digital check-in, police registration form, access information, requests during the stay, departure instructions, review request. No app, no account.

items.q: What is sent automatically?
items.a: Messages are triggered by stay events: the confirmation, the approach of arrival, the handover of access details, departure, the review. You define the content and the timing; they go out without anyone having to think about it.

items.q: Does digital check-in replace the front desk?
items.a: It relieves the front desk of data entry, not of welcoming guests. The guest enters their identity details and police registration form before arriving; the front desk receives them instead of having them fill in forms. In a riad without a permanent front desk, this makes even more of a difference.

items.q: Can you sell services during the stay?
items.a: Yes: upgrades, breakfast, spa, transfers, late check-out. The request becomes an assigned task and a line on the bill, with no re-entry. This is where revenue beyond accommodation is made.

items.q: What about guests who speak neither French nor Arabic?
items.a: The assistant supports about a dozen languages with translation. Your team reads and replies in their own.

items.q: Which channels come into the inbox?
items.a: WhatsApp, Booking, Expedia, Airbnb and direct email. Each message joins the thread of the relevant stay, so you don't have to piece together a conversation scattered across four extranets.

items.q: Does AI reply instead of my team?
items.a: It suggests replies and handles routine requests; you stay in control of what matters. The settings define what goes out automatically and what goes through approval: the level of autonomy is yours.

items.q: In which languages?
items.a: Guests are supported in about a dozen languages, with translation. Field teams receive their assignments in French or Arabic, depending on what they actually use.

items.q: Can a message become a task?
items.a: Yes, and that is the difference with a simple unified inbox. A request for towels or a breakdown report becomes an assigned task with an owner and a deadline, instead of staying a message someone has to remember to deal with.

items.q: What happens when nobody replies?
items.a: Reminders and escalations follow the rules you have defined. The point is not reply speed in itself, but that no request gets lost in a thread.

items.q: Does Sojori connect to Mews?

items.q: What is MCP, and why would a PMS use it?
items.a: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets an AI, such as ChatGPT, Claude or an in-house agent, read application data and use it to answer. Applied to a PMS, it means asking a question in plain language and getting an answer built on your actual figures, without exporting a file or opening a dashboard. The difference with a classic API: you have nothing to develop, the AI knows how to use the server on its own.

items.q: Does my data go to OpenAI or Anthropic?

What circulates are operating figures: occupancy, revenue, delays, channel mix.

items.q: Why is guest identity excluded by design?
items.a: Because a protection that relies on a filter always ends up being bypassed. We chose the opposite: identifying fields are not in the data the server can read. There is nothing to filter, so nothing to forget to filter. Law 09-08 on the protection of personal data applies to your guests; we would rather have the architecture answer the question than a promise.

items.q: Can the AI change anything?
items.a: No. The server is read-only in this scope: the AI reads, analyses and reports. It does not create a reservation, change a price or assign a task. Actions go through the interfaces where there is a trace and someone accountable.

items.q: How can you tell whether a figure given by the AI is reliable?
items.a: Each answer states the period actually covered by the data. If you ask for a two-year comparison and the mirror only starts eight months ago, the server flags it rather than producing an incomplete figure that looks complete. This is the main cause of errors when you connect an AI to a business database.

comparatif-pms-maroc.k011: There is no best hotel software in absolute terms, and any comparison claiming otherwise is selling something. The Moroccan market splits into three families. International platforms like Cloudbeds offer worldwide coverage and a broad ecosystem. Moroccan vendors — Pluriel, Nozoul, Welcomax — natively handle the police registration form, the tourist tax, the dirham and Arabic, with local support. Finally, orchestration engines like Sojori sit at a different level: they include a PMS but their purpose is to trigger what follows the booking — housekeeping, maintenance, guest messages, pricing — and they connect to existing PMS rather than requiring a replacement. The right criterion is not the length of the feature list, but what costs you the most today.

comparatif-pms-maroc.k017: Most hoteliers compare feature lists. It is the surest way to pick a tool that is too broad, too expensive and in the end little used. The useful question lies elsewhere: what costs you the most today?

If it is coordination — rooms not ready on arrival, housekeeping organized by phone, maintenance that drags on, guest messages lost in a personal WhatsApp group — then no PMS will fix it, because that is not its job. That is precisely when orchestration becomes relevant.

pms-tanger.k012: A hotel PMS in Tangier has to absorb a considerable gap in activity between summer and the rest of the year. pms-tanger.k014: Tangier has a very busy summer — Moroccan diaspora, Spanish tourists arriving across the strait, cruise passengers — followed by a long quiet period. The occupancy gap between August and January is wider than what Casablanca or Rabat experience.
pms-tanger.k015: This amplitude has a concrete consequence: the summer team is partly seasonal. An operation that relies on the experience of a manager present all year round falls apart in July, when recent reinforcements are the ones carrying out the work. Tasks triggered automatically and sent on WhatsApp do not depend on that memory.
pms-tanger.k016: Which operations should you centralize in Tangier?
pms-tanger.k017: The stay record holds the dates, the room, the source, the guests, the payments and the invoice. At the seaside, seasonal services are added — transfer, beach, dining — that exist only three months a year.
pms-tanger.k018: The critical point remains room turnaround in high season: with occupancy close to the maximum, a room that is not ready delays an arrival, and there is no spare room to absorb the delay.
